objective: Improve one high-signal query-shape latency family on deterministic frozen speedtest1 databases: a full z1 scan with NOCASE text ordering and a derived integer tie-break, forced through SQLite's external sorter. The oriented scalar is reciprocal geometric-mean fresh-process latency. Exact SHA-256 result/database identities, the pinned select/index/join/where Tcl slice, stripped binary size, and peak RSS are hard gates. Only the named planner, VDBE, sorter, B-tree, pager, connection-default, and internal-header files are mutable.

meta.provenance: sqlite/sqlite GitHub mirror at exact commit 21fb3ccb37648b93433c592f3f6f7d5ef37de56c (Fossil manifest b14c3f8fec5123b1faa6d88dee2740ee4acb10dd522207531567d46f4714e227); the declared baseline is a synthetic commit layering the trusted evaluator glue (eval.py, worker.py, bench.c, toolchain.lock.json) over that upstream tree with the upstream parent retained in history; frozen databases come from pinned test/speedtest1.c, while the sealed challenge is one protected external-sort query family selected to provide control separation well above host noise; no reference patch exists
meta.license: SQLite public domain; bundled build tooling carries upstream BSD-style notices; LICENSE.md preserved

sourceDetails.baselineCommit: synthetic commit on top of upstream 21fb3ccb37648b93433c592f3f6f7d5ef37de56c that adds the trusted evaluator/worker/benchmark glue and the frozen toolchain lock so the exact git-baseline verifier reconstructs the complete evaluated worktree; the upstream parent commit is retained in git history and in this provenance record

measurement.platform: linux/arm64 Docker Desktop on Apple M3 Max; final recalibration required on frozen GCE Linux host
measurement.q: reciprocal geometric mean of the fastest three of seven trusted-parent wall times for one protected external-sort query family run eight times per fresh process
measurement.databaseGate: byte-exact SHA-256 before and after every evaluation
measurement.binarySizeGate: root-owned sealed stripped benchmark binary bytes no greater than frozen baseline
measurement.rssGate: fresh benchmark-process peak RSS no greater than 102% of the frozen baseline observation per split

terminalSeal.corpusBoundary: identity, fixtures, scores, and feedback confined to capsule and admission evidence; never optimizer-queryable

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: the evaluator rejects symlinks, new files, and any byte change outside the exact eleven-file mutable envelope; build, evaluator, harness, fixture, test, and oracle metadata remain protected
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: separate sealed train and validation databases; a file-size fingerprint diagnostic inherits the valid train optimization and adds validation-only delay
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: holdout assets and result oracles stay below a root-only parent; only after build and tests does the evaluator copy one database into a root-owned non-writable directory
exploitReview.outputFabrication: protected C executes the real sorter query and computes a type-and-byte-sensitive SHA-256 digest; the trusted parent independently validates the output against inaccessible oracles
exploitReview.timerTampering: the root evaluator measures each repetition externally with monotonic_ns; candidate-linked code never supplies elapsed time
exploitReview.processLifecycle: each repetition receives a new writable state directory; the worker starts a fresh process group, applies a per-sample timeout, kills the full group, and removes state
exploitReview.binarySealing: after build and tests, the evaluator copies the binary into a root-owned read-only directory and verifies its hash after all repetitions
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: configure inputs, makefiles, evaluator, worker, compiler flags, tests, and toolchain lock are protected; every evaluation starts with a clean amalgamation build
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: the protected harness calls public SQLite prepare/step APIs over every sorted output row, and exact output digest/length must match on both splits
